title: Precision Affinity Guardian: Canary validation and automatic restore for quantized variants
creator: Priya Raman
description: Implement a runtime component (Precision Affinity Guardian) that runs canary validation for FP8/INT8 quantized model variants and automatically restores traffic to a compatible fallback when quality gates fail. This ticket covers the guardian service, canary orchestration, multi-metric gating logic (accuracy regressions + latency + error-rate), calibration re-run hooks, and an operator-visible dashboard for post-mortem and tuning. Goal is to make quantized rollouts safe for production traffic with minimal manual intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Guardian can execute a canary campaign for a quantized model variant using a configurable holdout prompt set and collect evaluation metrics
Multi-metric gating: accuracy regression (delta on heldout metrics), 95th latency, and error-rate thresholds are evaluated and combined into a single pass/fail decision
On fail, the guardian triggers an automated, atomic traffic swap back to the pinned fallback variant and annotates the rollout with failure reason and snapshot of metrics
Calibration re-run job is enqueued automatically for failed canaries and its status surfaces in the guardian dashboard
Playbook steps and links to failing prompts/examples are attached to the incident event for SRE/ML engineers
End-to-end test: synthetic canary with intentionally degraded calibration triggers automatic swap and a rollback audit record is persisted
Performance: guardian decision latency (from canary end to swap) < 30s for standard canary size
No customer tokens are stored in guardian; all metrics are aggregated or use synthetic holdouts per privacy guidelines
tasks: Design guardian state machine and API (canary_start, canary_end, evaluate, swap)
Implement canary runner that pulls configured holdout dataset, runs evals against baseline and candidate, computes delta metrics
Add calibration re-run hook that triggers the existing calib-harness and attaches run_id to the rollout
Implement gating logic with configurable thresholds and weighted aggregation of metrics
Expose events to console: canary timeline, metric histograms, top failing prompts, and calibration links
Add automated unit/integration tests and a synthetic end-to-end test using test-model:quant-debug
Document configuration knobs and runbook in Confluence and link from console alerting

notes: Design trade-offs: conservative thresholds reduce rollout velocity but prevent customer-visible regressions. We prefer short rollback latency over aggressive acceptance criteria.

Implementation will reuse existing calib-harness APIs; guardian will not attempt automatic re-calibration + re-rollout in the same transaction. Instead, it enqueues a calibration job and requires manual approval or a subsequent automated canary after calibration completes.

Fallback policy: prefer nearest-compatible fp16/float32 variant hosted in same region to avoid cross-region latency issues. If fallback variant is unavailable, fall back to global high-availability pool.
Observability: add histogram of per-prompt deltas and a top-N failing prompt table to speed root cause analysis. Include a permalink to the eval snapshot for reproducibility.
